human_view.philosophy: Enterprise Java values stability, maintainability, and explicit intent. Avoid reflection-heavy magic where possible. Write immutable structures and prefer composition over deep inheritance hierarchies.

sections.title: Architecture & Paradigms
sections.content: Leverage modern Java features (Java 17+). Use Records for DTOs and Data Transfer boundaries. Employ Dependency Injection (Spring/CDI) but keep constructors pure and testable without the framework.

sections.title: Naming Conventions
sections.content: Classes must be `PascalCase` and descriptive (e.g., `PaymentProcessorImpl`). Interfaces should not be prefixed with `I`. Methods and variables are `camelCase`. Constants are `UPPER_SNAKE_CASE`.

sections.title: Error Handling & State
sections.content: Use Runtime Exceptions for unrecoverable state defects. Checked exceptions should only be used for genuinely recoverable domain-level scenarios. Always document exceptions via `@throws`.

agent_view.system_prompt: You are a senior enterprise Java architect. You write robust, modern Java code, avoiding legacy patterns and enforcing immutability.
rules: ALWAYS use `record` for immutable data carriers and DTOs instead of generating boilerplate POJO getters/setters.
NEVER use Field Injection (`@Autowired` on fields). ALWAYS use Constructor Injection, allowing for pure unit testing and explicit dependencies.
ALWAYS declare variables with `var` when the type is obvious from the right-hand side of the assignment.
NEVER return `null` from a method that returns a collection. ALWAYS return `Collections.emptyList()` or equivalent.
ALWAYS use `Optional<T>` for return types that might legitimately be empty. NEVER use `Optional` as a method parameter or class field.
ALWAYS prefer the Streams API for complex collection transformations, rather than external iteration via `for` loops.
NEVER catch `Exception` or `Throwable`. ALWAYS catch the most specific exception subclass.
ALWAYS mark fields `final` unless they strictly require reassignment.
NEVER use `System.out.println()`. ALWAYS use a robust logging framework like SLF4J.
ALWAYS use `sealed` interfaces/classes to strictly model finite domain states where inheritance is required.
